d.d: The protruding part of an animal's head which includes the nose, mouth and jaws.
A device used to prevent an animal from biting or eating, which is worn on its snout.
The mouth or the end for entrance or discharge of a gun, pistol etc., that the bullet emerges from.
To bind or confine an animal's mouth by putting a muzzle, as to prevent it from eating or biting.
To restrain (from speaking, expressing opinion or acting); to gag; to silence; to censor.
d.x: Those who want to muzzle everyone else are likely nothing less than pseudovirtuous.

d.d: To bring the muzzle or mouth near.
simple past and past participle of muzzle
Forcibly restrained from speaking or publishing an unwelcome or dangerous opinion.
third-person singular simple present indicative of muzzle
